name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Build a self-review loop that runs after every prompt batch, flagging only high-impact changes to the lead. This keeps the system honest without drowning us in noise. Trade-off: we accept slower feedback for low-risk tweaks to avoid alert fatigue.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk is that "high-impact" is subjective until proven by failure—what’s high-impact to one lead is noise to another. A better alternative is to auto-apply *all* safe changes immediately, then log the rest for review only if the lead opts in. Settle it by running a 2-week trial: measure lead engagement with alerts vs. auto-applied changes, and let the data decide.
